title: occupancy-guided-slab-retention-and-pinned-span-eviction
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Improves KV cache memory efficiency and tail latency: occupancy-guided slab retention, pinned-span eviction watermark, shard-local freelist compaction. No API changes.
description:
Motivation: our paged KV cache sometimes retains low-occupancy slabs and holds pinned spans longer than necessary under mixed workloads (short chat vs long-context inference). This increases memory footprint and exacerbates tail latency during bursty traffic. This PR implements an occupancy-guided slab retention policy plus a pinned-span eviction watermark and local freelist compaction to reduce fragmentation and improve reuse latency.

Summary of changes (single paragraph): Implement occupancy histogram per slab class, a retention score used by the slab recycler to prefer evicting low-score slabs; introduce a pinned-span eviction watermark that allows background demotion of lightly-pinned spans when overall pool pressure exceeds threshold; add shard-local freelist compaction to coalesce adjacent free spans for fast single-op reallocation; expose a small allocator fastpath for contiguous single-span reuse that avoids lock handoffs; add lightweight kernel scheduling hints so the runtime's request scheduler deprioritizes long-running kernel launches when reclaim is in progress. Included unit tests, integration kv stress tests, and a benchmark harness run against the perf-canary image.

Design notes and rationale: occupancy histogram is kept per-slab-class (128/256/512/1k/2k) and sampled on free/alloc to avoid scan costs. Retention score = weighted(occupancy, last_access_ms, reuse_rate) which favors slabs with high reuse or recent access; this prevents thrashing for hot prefixes. The pinned-span watermark is adaptive: watermark = min(max_pinned, pool_size * pinned_ratio_threshold) and is tuned so background eviction only kicks in when the allocator cannot satisfy 95% of small allocations within the usual fastpath window. Shard-local freelist compaction reduces cross-shard fragmentation and keeps the critical path lock-free for the common allocation case. Kernel scheduling hints are exposed as a small integer tag on reclaim work so the request scheduler can push reclaim off the hot GPU queue.

Benchmarks: microbenchmarks run on perf-canary (A100-equivalent), mixed workload (60% short generations, 40% long-context streaming) with continuous batching enabled. Results: 99th p90 latency for short calls reduced from 72ms -> 66ms (~8.3% tail reduction); median latency for long-context improved 5.7%; overall throughput (tokens/sec) improved ~6.1% under the same GPU occupancy; resident set size across runs reduced by ~7% on average for our test corpus. Benchmarks include 1000-run averages and 95% CI reported in commit.

Compatibility and rollouts: default behavior is opt-in via a runtime config flag (runtime.kv.occupancy_retention = true) to allow staged rollout; however the cluster-level default for new images in staging is enabled. No changes to public API surface. Configs documented in redwood/docs/ops/kv-allocator.md.

Testing & CI: initial CI run failed on a flaky freelist compact race in unit allocator_test.cc (see review thread). Added a targeted repro and fixed with a brief critical-section reorder and an atomic fence in commit "fix: freelist compact race and add repro". After that, CI passed (all checks green). Additional long-running soak on perf-canary for 12h showed stable memory and pending-io metrics.

Risk and mitigations: background demotion of pinned spans could surface latency spikes if tuned too aggressively; we default to conservative thresholds and added a circuit-breaker that disables demotion under sustained ENFORCING allocation failures. The kernel-scheduling hints are informational; schedulers that ignore them will see no difference.
